Before we start

What your business needs in place.

None of this is code, and each one decides how fast you launch.

A commercial registration, for payments

Payment gateways in Egypt and Saudi will not settle to an individual. If it is not done yet, start it today; it is usually the longest wait in the whole launch.

A business bank account

In the same name as the registration, so settlement does not fail the day your first orders arrive.

What you sell, written down

Products or services, prices and a few lines about each. I shape the copy; I cannot invent the offer.

One person who decides

Fast answers keep the timeline. A package that waits a week for every approval takes three times as long.

Terms

How the money and the risk are split.

No retainer to start a conversation, and no invoice for work that never got delivered.

Half to start, half on delivery

Balance falls due when the work is done and handed over. Not delivered, not charged.

Fixed price, not an estimate

The number holds unless you change the scope. If I misjudged it, that is mine.

The clock starts at handover

From the day I have everything on the list, not from the day you pay.

One round of revisions included

Then hourly, quoted before anything starts. No surprise invoices.

You own everything at the end

Code, accounts, assets and credentials. Nothing is held hostage.

What you send

The handover, in one list.

Send it in one go and the clock starts.

  • Business name, logo and colours, or permission to make simple ones
  • What you sell: products or services, with prices
  • Photos you own, or the go-ahead to use licensed stock
  • The domain you want, or two or three you would accept
  • Commercial registration and bank details, for payments
  • For Build: a description of the product in your own words, however rough

How it runs

Six steps, and you see each one.

  1. 01

    Discovery call

    An hour on what the business sells and to whom. You leave with the scope for your budget in writing.

  2. 02

    Accounts first

    Domain, email, WhatsApp, payment gateway and store accounts — started on day one, because their approvals take the longest.

  3. 03

    Design

    The look and the main screens, shown to you before anything is built.

  4. 04

    Build

    Site or store, flows and automations — and for Build, the product and its dashboard. A preview link every week.

  5. 05

    Test with real money

    A real order, a real payment, a real WhatsApp confirmation, end to end.

  6. 06

    Launch and hand over

    Live on your domain and in the stores, every account in your name, and a walkthrough for running it.

Scope

  • Paid advertising and its budget

Right fit, wrong fit

Saves a call that would end in no.

A good fit

  • You are starting a business and want it done once, properly
  • You have a budget and want to know exactly what it buys
  • You sell in Arabic and English, in Egypt or Saudi
  • You want to run it yourself afterwards

Not a fit

  • You need a large platform with many user types — see Enterprise Systems
  • You want the cheapest possible website, not a working business setup
  • You have no product or service decided yet
  • You need advertising more than you need a setup

After launch

After you open.

Launch includes 30 days of care and Build includes 60. In that time anything I built that breaks is fixed at no cost. After it, the Care plan keeps someone on call for updates, fixes and the monthly numbers, or you run it yourself; either way, everything is already in your name.

Questions

The ones people actually ask.

Is the price really fixed?

Yes. The first call fits the scope to the budget, and that scope is written down. If I underestimated it, that is mine to absorb. If you add to it, the addition is quoted before it starts.

Can I start with Launch and move to Build later?

Yes. Build reuses everything Launch set up, so nothing is thrown away. The move is quoted on what is left to do, not on the full $5,000.

What will I pay every month after launch?

Only the running costs, which go directly to the providers: usually hosting or Shopify, WhatsApp messaging and payment fees. I list them for you before we start. The Care plan is optional.

How do I pay?

Half to start and half on delivery. You can pay in USD, EGP or SAR.

Why not hire separate freelancers for each part?

You can, and the pieces often do not connect: the store does not talk to WhatsApp, and nobody owns the gap between them. Here, one person is accountable for all of it working together.
